cohort: The study included women with singleton pregnancies diagnosed with gestational diabetes who delivered after 34 weeks of gestation in a university-affiliated medical center between 2012 and 2016.
finding: Corticosteroid treatment for diabetic mothers was not associated with neonatal adverse outcomes, but was found to be associated with a lower birth weight, when delivery occurred after 34 weeks of gestation.
birth_weight: Birth weight was significantly lower in women treated with corticosteroids (2486 vs. 2675 g, p = 0.02 at late-preterm, and 3160 vs. 3319 g, p < 0.001 at term).
gest_age: The study included deliveries after 34 weeks of gestation, categorized as late-preterm (34+0 to 36+6 weeks) and term (37+0 to 41+6 weeks).
